statement.en: This level is set in Saskatchewan. Discover Canada says the province was once called the breadbasket of the world, and the wheat province. It is Canada's largest grower of grains and oilseeds, and it has the world's richest deposits of uranium and potash. Regina, the capital, is where the Royal Canadian Mounted Police train.
statement.fr: Ce niveau se déroule en Saskatchewan. Découvrir le Canada rappelle qu'on appelait autrefois la province le grenier du monde et la province du blé. Elle est la plus grande productrice de céréales et d'oléagineux au Canada, et elle possède les gisements d'uranium et de potasse les plus riches du monde. C'est à Regina, la capitale, que s'entraîne la Gendarmerie royale du Canada.

source.quote: is the country’s largest producer of grains and oilseeds. It also boasts the world’s richest deposits of uranium and potash

verification.evidence: Saskatchewan, once known as the “breadbasket of the world” and the “wheat province,” has 40% of the arable land in Canada and is the country’s largest producer of grains and oilseeds. It also boasts the world’s richest deposits of uranium and potash, used in fertilizer, and produces oil and natural gas. Regina, the capital, is home to the training academy of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.

blurb.en: In 1951, for the first time, most Canadians could afford enough food, a home and clothing. Before that year, many could not.
blurb.fr: En 1951, pour la première fois, la majorité des Canadiens pouvaient se payer assez de nourriture, un logement et des vêtements. Avant cette année-là, beaucoup n'y arrivaient pas.

source.quote: In 1951, for the first time, a majority of Canadians were able to afford adequate food, shelter and clothing.

verification.evidence: In 1951, for the first time, a majority of Canadians were able to afford adequate food, shelter and clothing.

blurb.en: After the Second World War Canada's economy grew quickly. Today Canadians have one of the highest standards of living in the world, built on hard work and on trade with other countries.
blurb.fr: Après la Seconde Guerre mondiale, l'économie du Canada a connu une forte croissance. Aujourd'hui, les Canadiens ont l'un des meilleurs niveaux de vie au monde, grâce au travail et au commerce avec d'autres pays.

source.quote: Today, Canadians enjoy one of the world's highest standards of living— maintained by the hard work of Canadians and by trade with other nations, in particular the United States.

verification.evidence: Between 1945 and 1970, as Canada drew closer to the United States and other trading partners, the country enjoyed one of the strongest economies among industrialized nations. Today, Canadians enjoy one of the world’s highest standards of living— maintained by the hard work of Canadians and by trade with other nations, in particular the United States.

blurb.en: This combine is cutting standing grain and leaving stubble. A machine like this one burns fuel all day. Oil was found in Alberta in 1947, and that discovery started Canada's modern energy industry.
blurb.fr: Cette moissonneuse-batteuse coupe le grain sur pied et laisse du chaume. Une machine comme celle-ci brûle du carburant toute la journée. Du pétrole a été découvert en Alberta en 1947, et cette découverte a lancé l'industrie énergétique moderne du Canada.

source.quote: The discovery of oil in Alberta in 1947 began Canada’s modern energy industry.

verification.evidence: The discovery of oil in Alberta in 1947 began Canada’s modern energy industry.

blurb.en: Trains run to a timetable. Sir Sandford Fleming worked out the system of standard time zones that the whole world still uses.
blurb.fr: Les trains circulent selon un horaire. Sir Sandford Fleming a mis au point le système de fuseaux horaires standards que le monde entier utilise encore.

source.quote: Sir Sandford Fleming — invented the worldwide system of standard time zones.

verification.evidence: Sir Sandford Fleming — invented the worldwide system of standard time zones.
